instructions: Put the rice, 3 cups of water and 1/2 tsp of the salt in a medium pot over high heat. Bring it to a boil, then cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on until the shrimp are done.
Meanwhile, finely chop the onion and the bell pepper. Slice 3 celery stalks thin and mince the garlic.
Pat the shrimp dry. Toss them in a bowl with 1/4 tsp of the salt and the pepper and put them in the fridge.

Heat the oil in a large deep skillet over medium-high heat. Add the onion, bell pepper, celery and the last 1/4 tsp salt. Turn the heat down to medium and cook for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring now and then, until the vegetables are very soft.
Add the garlic, Creole seasoning, thyme, cayenne and bay leaf. Stir for 30 seconds, until it smells toasty.
Add the tomato sauce, 1 cup of water and the Worcestershire. Bring it to a boil, then turn the heat to low and simmer, uncovered, for 8 to 10 minutes, until the sauce thickens.
Add the shrimp and stir them into the sauce. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until they're pink and curled into a loose C.
Take the pan off the heat. Fish out the bay leaf and stir in 2 tbsp chopped parsley. Cut the lemon into wedges.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt or a squeeze of the lemon.
Serve over the rice with the lemon wedges and the hot sauce on the table.
method_notes: Lead is From a Chef's Kitchen (4.57 from 221), a no-roux Creole built on onion, pepper and celery, Creole seasoning and a tomato sauce simmer, with the shrimp added last. Pinch and Swirl, Simply Stacie and Foodiecrush agree on the vegetable base and the quick finish; they use canned diced tomatoes and some add flour or cornstarch. Butter is replaced with more oil to keep it dairy-free, the Worcestershire is gluten-free, and the cayenne is cut to 1/4 tsp with hot sauce left for the table. Rice is added so the timeline includes it. Check the Creole seasoning label for gluten.
